analysis:
Integration of 13 units: the PR is CI-only (composite actions provider-ci-build and provider-release-build, ci-master.yml, desktop.yml, landing.yml, provider-release-cache.yml, provider-tests.yml, scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py) plus docs and a changelog. No provider runtime, wire protocol, attestation, key custody or encrypted prefix-cache code changed, so TB-002/003/007/009/011 and T-041 are unaffected in code. I replayed the patch text for provider-ci-build, provider-release-build and ci-master.yml and verified the earlier analyses against it.

Changed behavior:
1. A 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step writes CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off to GITHUB_ENV when RUNNER_NAME is darkbloom-* and DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL is empty. Only a constant string is written, so there is no injection. Every actions/cache restore and save step in the replayed actions and ci-master is gated on env.CI_ACTIONS_CACHE != 'off'. Save steps are gated too, so a skipped restore cannot lead to a save. This narrows exposure to GitHub's cache from sandbox hosts and supports the T-034/T-054 (A-011, A-017) build-integrity posture.
2. The restored .git validation now rejects a symlink or non-directory .git, any symlink inside it, non-sample hooks, and a config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include. git config --file only parses, so the check executes nothing. It also runs fsck. This is stricter than the base, which only ran fsck.

Residual hardening gap, not a regression: the config check is a denylist. Keys such as filter.*.process, core.sshCommand, credential.helper and diff.external are not screened. Exploiting it needs a prior poisoned write to the master/dev cache scope. Saves are limited to SAVE_CACHES on master/dev pushes, and PRs restore only.

Unverified, which is why deeper review is requested:
- The replay is incomplete (61 of 119 units). The head text of the later provider-tests.yml jobs, the desktop, landing and provider-release-cache workflows, and the action.yml pieces for provider-ci-products were not all supplied. Whether they get the same unsafe-.git check and gating is unconfirmed.
- The test script only pins strings. Actual enforcement lies in the YAML.
- The release workflows are said never to skip caches. The Blacksmith runner assumption and the DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL plane contract are external.

No concrete regression is supported by the evidence.
